audits.title: 1575 IMPROVING THE QUALITY OF COMPREHENSIVE GERIATRIC ASSESSMENT THROUGH INCORPORATION OF SKIN ASSESSMENT
audits.standard: Skin assessment as part of comprehensive geriatric assessment documented by doctors
audits.setting: Two geriatric wards, Southend University Hospital

cycle1.result: 15.8% of skin assessments documented by doctors (80.7% by nurses).

audits.intervention: Three PDSA cycles over 6 weeks: informal teaching at morning meeting, formal teaching by tissue viability nurse, and a reminder poster with escalation contacts.

cycle2.result: After PDSA 3, 8.8% of skin assessments completed.

audits.other_findings: PDSA 1 raised completion to 31.6% but PDSA 2 fell to 11.9%; authors suggest regular teaching every rotation.
audits.citation: Ali L, Kaneshamoorthy M, Haddadeen M, Salotun F, Krasniqi L. 1575 IMPROVING THE QUALITY OF COMPREHENSIVE GERIATRIC ASSESSMENT THROUGH INCORPORATION OF SKIN ASSESSMENT. Age and Ageing. 2023;52(Supplement_2). doi:10.1093/ageing/afad104.008.

audits.title: An audit of pressure ulcer incidence in a palliative care setting.
audits.standard: Pressure ulcer incidence; Waterlow risk assessment
audits.setting: Inpatient Unit, St Margaret's Somerset Hospice, specialist palliative care unit

cycle1.result: 26.1% admitted with pressure ulcers and 12.0% developed pressure damage during stay; 95.3% accurately assessed at high or very high risk on Waterlow; 89.2% of ulcers Grade 1 or 2.

audits.other_findings: 78.4% of developing ulcers were sacral; superficial ulcers often developed in the last days of life.
audits.citation: Galvin J. An audit of pressure ulcer incidence in a palliative care setting. Int J Palliat Nurs. 2002;8(5):214-221. doi:10.12968/ijpn.2002.8.5.10368. PMID: 12048504.

audits.title: A pressure ulcer audit and feedback project across multi-hospital settings in the Netherlands.
audits.standard: Adequate pressure ulcer prevention for high-risk patients and enabling conditions; case-mix-adjusted prevalence of grade 2 or higher pressure ulcers

cycle1.result: Baseline prevalence survey (figures not given in abstract).

audits.intervention: Hospital-specific performance data, national aggregate data and peer comparisons fed back after each annual survey.

cycle2.result: Case-mix-adjusted prevalence of pressure ulcers decreased over 5 years while the percentage of patients receiving adequate prevention and the number of enabling conditions increased.

audits.other_findings: More enabling conditions were associated with lower adjusted prevalence (chi2 = 125).
audits.citation: Bours GJ, Halfens RJ, Candel MJ, Grol RT, Abu-Saad HH. A pressure ulcer audit and feedback project across multi-hospital settings in the Netherlands. Int J Qual Health Care. 2004;16(3):211-218. doi:10.1093/intqhc/mzh034. PMID: 15150152.

audits.title: Tracking quality over time: what do pressure ulcer data show?
audits.standard: Pressure ulcer prevalence and prevention measures as quality markers

cycle1.result: Pressure ulcer prevalence 23.9% (8.0% excluding non-blanchable erythema).

audits.intervention: Comprehensive quality improvement programme (details not stated)

cycle2.result: Pressure ulcer prevalence 22.9% (12.0% excluding non-blanchable erythema).

audits.other_findings: Use of pressure-reducing mattresses increased while planned repositioning fell; little prevention documented on admission.
audits.citation: Gunningberg L, Stotts NA. Tracking quality over time: what do pressure ulcer data show?. Int J Qual Health Care. 2008;20(4):246-253. doi:10.1093/intqhc/mzn009. PMID: 18390902.

audits.title: Quality improvement program to reduce the prevalence of pressure ulcers in an intensive care unit.
audits.setting: Intensive care unit, North Shore Hospital, Sydney

cycle1.result: Baseline pressure ulcer prevalence 50%; appropriate allocation of pressure-relieving devices 75%.

audits.intervention: One-on-one clinical instruction to bedside nurses during skin surveys and display of pressure ulcer data in the clinical area.

cycle2.result: Prevalence fell to 8%; appropriate allocation of pressure-relieving devices rose to 95% to 100%.

audits.other_findings: 563 skin surveys over 22 audits; likely origin and anatomical site of ulcers did not change.
audits.citation: Elliott R, McKinley S, Fox V. Quality improvement program to reduce the prevalence of pressure ulcers in an intensive care unit. Am J Crit Care. 2008;17(4):328-34; quiz 335; discussion 336-7. doi:10.4037/ajcc2008.17.4.328. PMID: 18593831.

audits.title: Improving pressure ulcer risk assessment and management using the Waterlow scale at a London teaching hospital.
audits.standard: Waterlow pressure ulcer risk assessment scale
audits.setting: Inpatients at a London teaching hospital

cycle1.result: Nursing Waterlow score recorded for 81% of patients; nursing scores were lower than study scores.

audits.intervention: Staff questionnaires, educational sessions, presentations and posters on risk stratification.

cycle2.result: Nursing Waterlow score recorded for 100% of patients (p value truncated in abstract); differences between nursing and study scores reduced.

audits.other_findings: Cycle 1 under-scoring was mainly from failing to assess certain Waterlow categories; greater multidisciplinary input was still needed.
audits.citation: Mahalingam S, Gao L, Nageshwaran S, Vickers C, Bottomley T, Grewal P. Improving pressure ulcer risk assessment and management using the Waterlow scale at a London teaching hospital. J Wound Care. 2014;23(12):613-622. doi:10.12968/jowc.2014.23.12.613. PMID: 25492277.

audits.title: Effects of a pressure-ulcer audit and feedback regional programme at 1 and 2 years in nursing homes: A prospective longitudinal study.
audits.standard: Pressure ulcer preventive practices (repositioning, anti-decubitus mattress) and prevalence
audits.setting: Nursing homes of the Canton of Geneva

cycle1.result: Acquired pressure ulcer prevalence 4.5% in homes participating all 3 years.

audits.intervention: Oral and written feedback to nursing home reference nurses 2 months after each survey.

cycle2.result: Acquired pressure ulcer prevalence 2.9% (p 0.035); repositioning and anti-decubitus bed or mattress use improved significantly.

audits.other_findings: 27 homes took part in 2015 and 2016 (4607 patients across both years) and 15 in 2017; a 2016 survey was also done.
audits.citation: Righi L, Ourahmoune A, Béné N, Rae AC, Courvoisier DS, Chopard P. Effects of a pressure-ulcer audit and feedback regional programme at 1 and 2 years in nursing homes: A prospective longitudinal study. PLoS One. 2020;15(5):e0233471. doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0233471. PMID: 32469916.

audits.title: Pressure injury prevention practices among medical surgical nurses in a tertiary hospital: An observational and chart audit study.
audits.setting: Two medical and two surgical wards, tertiary hospital (Peking University First Hospital, per affiliations)

cycle1.result: Risk assessment on admission 100%; regular repositioning about 84% (n = 486); patient education documented in 75% (n = 433); skin care, nutritional screening and support surfaces suboptimal.

audits.other_findings: Surgical patients generally received and had documented better preventive care than medical patients.
audits.citation: Li Z, Marshall AP, Lin F, Ding Y, Chaboyer W. Pressure injury prevention practices among medical surgical nurses in a tertiary hospital: An observational and chart audit study. Int Wound J. 2022;19(5):1165-1179. doi:10.1111/iwj.13712. PMID: 34729917.

audits.title: Pressure ulcers: a clinical audit to determine compliance against the aSSKINg framework in an adult community nursing setting.
audits.setting: Adult community nursing service, Sussex Community NHS Foundation Trust, south-east England

cycle1.result: Overall compliance poor; only two criteria met: chair equipment provision and referral to tissue viability

audits.other_findings: Recommendations: mandatory pressure ulcer training, a larger tissue viability network and an aSSKINg template in the electronic record.

audits.title: Hospital-Acquired Pressure Injury Reduction: A Nurse-Led Quality Improvement Initiative in Qatar.
audits.standard: Aim to reduce HAPI incidence by 50% by September 2022; SSKIN care bundle

cycle1.result: Average 60±5 hospital-acquired pressure injuries per month, about 50% device-related.

audits.intervention: CUSP programme: staff training, electronic documentation review, spot audits of SSKIN bundle compliance, policy updates and more pressure-relieving devices.

cycle2.result: 64.4% reduction in HAPI incidence; 66% decrease in device-related pressure injuries.

audits.citation: Melhem T, Varadharajan V, Mcdonald IS, Al-Mutawa MN, George D, Thomas D, et al.. Hospital-Acquired Pressure Injury Reduction: A Nurse-Led Quality Improvement Initiative in Qatar. Cureus. 2025;17(4):e81726. doi:10.7759/cureus.81726. PMID: 40322337.

audits.title: Development of an Interdisciplinary Healthcare Team for Pressure Injury Management: A Quality Improvement Project.
audits.standard: Staff adherence to plan of care (audit tool) and hospital-acquired pressure injury rate
audits.setting: Medical adult inpatient units, private tertiary hospital (Johns Hopkins Aramco Healthcare), Eastern Province
audits.intervention: Interdisciplinary pressure injury team formed, unit-based education sessions and quarterly prevalence surveys (February 21 to May 23, 2017).

cycle2.result: HAPI rate 5%; 100% staff adherence to the plan of care.

audits.title: Increasing Nursing Documentation Efficiency With Wearable Sensors for Pressure Injury Prevention.

cycle1.result: Mean documented repositioning interval 6.6 hours; documentation compliance 31%.

audits.intervention: Wearable sensor system providing automatic repositioning documentation.

cycle2.result: Mean repositioning interval 2.4 hours; documentation compliance 82%.

audits.other_findings: Total convenience sample 105 records; in patients with obesity the interval fell from 9.4 to 2.5 hours.
audits.citation: Rose A, Cooley A, Yap TL, Alderden J, Sabol VK, Lin JA, et al.. Increasing Nursing Documentation Efficiency With Wearable Sensors for Pressure Injury Prevention. Crit Care Nurse. 2022;42(2):14-22. doi:10.4037/ccn2022116. PMID: 35362082.

audits.title: Reducing the Pressure: Improving the Safety of Adult Inpatients at an Urban Hospital by Reducing Pressure Injury Incidence.
audits.standard: Goal of pressure injury incidence of 20% using best practice guidelines and toolkits
audits.setting: Adult inpatients at an urban hospital

cycle1.result: Baseline pressure injury incidence 40%; prevention score 45%; skin assessment documentation 35%.

audits.intervention: SBARW (Situation, Background, Assessment, Recommendations, Wounds) report sheets, turn clocks and team engagement over four PDSA cycles.

cycle2.result: Pressure injury incidence 17%; mean prevention score 74%; skin assessment documentation 95%.

audits.citation: Burpee LH, Schaeffer AM. Reducing the Pressure: Improving the Safety of Adult Inpatients at an Urban Hospital by Reducing Pressure Injury Incidence. J Dr Nurs Pract. 2024;17(3):148-156. doi:10.1891/jdnp-2023-0024. PMID: 39537325.
